title: Basic Commands [chown]
description:
# chown
`chown` stands for `change owner`. It changes who owns a file.
```bash
chown user:group filepath
```
- `user` - the new owner
- `group` - the new group

You need `sudo` to change ownership to another user.


---
## Assignment:
Locking permissions isn't enough - you're still the owner. Anyone with `sudo` could just `chmod` it back. Transfer ownership to `root` so even you need sudo to touch it. Plausible deniability.

Run `sudo chown root:root` on the offshore file. Submit in the root of the project.
